sections.title: Employment Contract
sections.text:
S.E.E.S. member Aigis looks like an ordinary girl when walking through the school grounds.

What distant place will she walk toward?

sections.title: Token
sections.text: A red ribbon, tied into a bow. Even in a combat stance, she will never let it come loose. Is this a skill befitting a machine? No one knows the answer.

sections.title: Student Overview
sections.text:
Aigis. Registered in March of 1102 at the Atrium Notary Office as a Category III resident; admitted to Saint Marcel Comprehensive School pursuant to Article 36 of the appendix to the Charter of Lateran Citizens' Rights and Chapter 2, Article 5 of the Regulations on the Administration of Entrants.
Teacher's remarks: Aigis is bright and eager to learn, earnest and rigorous, full of a sense of responsibility, and strict with herself. She has achieved notable results in the firearm-like armament course series. It is hoped that she will open her heart a little more and try more group activities, so that alongside her academic progress she may also enjoy a rich school life.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
After enrolling, Aigis drew considerable attention from her classmates for her performance in the firearm-like armament courses. She is not Sankta, yet she carries and skillfully wields several weapons resembling firearms. At the end of one such class, Sesa from the neighboring class asked whether what she used were the rumored Columbian-made replica firearms, and whether her distinctive grip had something to do with that. Aigis answered these questions with the utmost seriousness—and it was not hard to tell that neither the one answering nor the one asking understood a word the other was saying.
Dr.{@nickname}, passing by, listened in silence for five minutes to the two students talking entirely past each other, then took over the conversation—from the replica firearms of Columbian security firms, to an experimental weapon that had briefly appeared in Sargon, to the differences between Iberian hand cannons and Lateran launchers, and even to the research Closure of the mechanics club had once attempted. Sesa listened with rapt attention, having quite forgotten the question he had originally put to Aigis. Aigis, too, heard out the Doctor's impromptu lecture on developing firearm-like equipment with equal seriousness, and light flickered in her eyes now and then.
After the lecture, Aigis followed Dr.{@nickname} all the way to the office door. The teacher turned and asked, "Do you have any other questions, Aigis?" She answered, "I have committed everything you just said to memory. Also—you were getting me out of an awkward spot just now, weren't you? Thank you." After a brief hesitation she continued, "I would like to ask one more thing. Are those weapons you mentioned very similar to my own configuration? In what respects, specifically..."
The teacher seemed not to have expected Aigis to say that; he paused for a second, then answered, "No. You and they are not the same." Then the teacher appeared to blink (it was impossible to be sure, with the hood and mask) and added, "That said, if you need maintenance on your equipment, you might talk to Closure in the mechanics club. She should be able to help."

One of the notes stuck to this page: At Dr.{@nickname}'s request, Closure's "technical correspondence" is attached to this file.
The second note stuck to this page: Amiya, you needn't black out the parts where Closure complains about me in her letter—if it's mistaken for some kind of technical secret, that would defeat the purpose. Simply record that Aigis uses non-Lateran replica firearms; that will do.

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
After their volunteer work at the Dessert Hall, the transfer students took to spending their free time there now and then. Aigis seemed rather fond of sweets—though not on account of the taste. As she put it: "Through my observations over this period, I have determined the reason Lateran people are so devoted to sweets."
"I'd wondered about that too—I think it's because Laterano produces a lot of sugar crops..." This was Ken's take.
"Huh? Isn't it that Lateran people love sweets, and that's why they grow those crops?" This was Yukari's view.
"So it comes down to a tradition of taste after all..." This was Fuuka's guess.
"No—the key is energy supply efficiency." Aigis said with confidence. "Sugars are the brain's primary and most direct source of energy, and ingesting sugar supplies the brain with energy at the greatest possible speed. That is why Lateran people favor sweets so highly: as an energy-supplying substance, they hold an absolute advantage."
"..." This was Makoto's contribution.
Aigis confirmed her own conclusion. "Laterano indeed. Order is well kept, and efficiency is extraordinary."
There was a trace of resignation on Yukari's face. "Efficient, sure, it does seem efficient... But when it comes to 'order,' maybe Lateran people understand it a bit differently than we do? Laterano has plenty of 'rules,' but things like a 'Public Building Demolition Ordinance'... I'm pretty sure our world doesn't have rules like that..."
Aigis did not notice Yukari's remark; she seemed to have moved on to another question. "But there is one thing I do not understand. When Keira and Itida were arguing earlier, they said sweets are the memories of Lateran people. If a sufficient quantity of energy powder were added to sugar-free ice cream, the ice cream would become a more efficient food, and if everyone ate sugar-free ice cream with energy powder added, corresponding memories would form as well. In that case, could sugar-free ice cream with energy powder not simply replace sweets?"
Ken frowned as he turned Aigis's words over, and Fuuka said, a little uncertainly, "Um... memories and remembrances aren't quite the same thing, are they...?"
Aigis still seemed to have doubts, but at that point Makoto nodded.
"'Memory' and 'remembrance' are different... I see. No—I would like to think about this a while longer." That was what Aigis said in the end.

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
The details of the Requiem Funeral Hall incident have still not been disclosed, but that did not stop the transfer students from forming a good relationship with the two funeral hall attendants they met during volunteer work. On one day off, the transfer students went with Giada to help Giulio, who until then had been living in the returnees' apartments, move house. Aigis was very keen on this, declaring, "Leave the hauling to me. There will be no mishaps."
The trouble came from Giulio. At the new place, as he unpacked the luggage he had brought back from Columbia, he produced in turn a Chinese checkers set, three sketchbooks, two seat cushions, and a broken party blower—with an expression of utter astonishment. He seemed to have no recollection of more than half the items in his own luggage, and Aigis had no choice but to wait while he checked them one by one.
Aigis found this quite incomprehensible: clearly these items were not necessary to Giulio's life, so why carry them all that way home? She added that so long as she had sufficient power, she could survive on her own in the vast majority of environments, without needing any external possessions at all.
Giulio explained apologetically that he had been in low spirits when he left Columbia, and had only thrown a few things together in a hurry at the Executor's prompting—so he had not paid attention to what went into the luggage.
"Still," said Giulio, "I do have to thank him. If I'd simply left these things behind... I think I'd be regretting it right now." Looking at the game board, the sketchbooks, the cushions and the blower, he smiled fondly.
Aigis was about to ask more when a knock at the door interrupted her. The visitor was a pale-blond Executor; Giulio greeted him warmly and introduced him as the very Executor he had mentioned earlier, whom he had invited to the housewarming meal. Recalling Giulio's explanation from a moment before, Aigis put a question to the Executor:
"Executor, did you tell Mr. Giulio to pack these items because they were needed for the journey home?"
"It is not necessary."
"Do you understand what they are for?"
"I do not."
"...Then why did you have Mr. Giulio carry these items? Would travelling light not be more efficient?"
"I agree. I am sufficient in myself to guarantee the citizen's safe return to Laterano. But after returning, the citizen must go on living his life, and he may need certain items whose use I do not understand. So, in my capacity as an Executor, I fulfilled my duty to remind him."
Aigis's questions were not entirely resolved, but she seemed to think highly of the way this Executor conducted himself, and enjoyed a lively conversation with a man famous for being poor at communication.
Looked at this way, even if the volunteer work gave Aigis nothing to go on in choosing a career, it at least helped her make friends.

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
At Dr.{@nickname}'s suggestion, the transfer students visited the Reliquary together once before leaving Laterano.
By the rules of the Reliquary, people may pray to the relic by spraying graffiti on it—or, put another way, make a wish. The transfer students were a little awkward on arriving, but happily the atmosphere was far more relaxed than they had imagined. Ken looked uneasy about writing on a holy relic, and Yukari reassured him bluntly: "When in Rome. Look, the graffiti's already layered a dozen deep—we just do it the way people here do." Fuuka examined the relic closely while she sprayed, and once she had come down she quietly asked Dr.{@nickname}, "Doctor, this... this is a machine, isn't it?" The teacher thought for a moment and told her, "It doesn't matter anymore."
Makoto did not spray a wish onto the relic. He gave Dr.{@nickname} a small smile and said something quietly. The teacher nodded to him.
The teacher passed the spray can to Aigis, who stood at the back, and asked, "Is there a wish you would like to make, Aigis?"
Aigis took the spray can, but seemed to hesitate. She looked at the relic and gazed at the riot of color on its surface. From where she stood, an ordinary person could hardly make out all the words and images upon it—but perhaps Aigis could.
At last she stepped forward. She did not leave a bold, brilliant piece of graffiti the way Lateran people do; it seemed she wrote only one small line of prayer.
Returning to her companions, she handed the spray can back to Dr.{@nickname}. Though he had asked about her wish a moment earlier, this time the teacher did not press further. Everyone has such moments—some wishes one would rather keep to oneself.
Aigis seemed to have something more she wanted to ask, but in the end she said nothing. She looked at the relic again, sunlight falling on her through the dome. Perhaps she already knew: the relic does not answer.

sections.title: Encrypted Report
sections.text:
There are so many mysteries surrounding Aigis that I hardly know where to begin... Let us start with her identity. Aigis and her companions have not gone to much trouble to hide it: Aigis is not an ordinary human—or, if you prefer, "not human" at all, given that she calls herself an "Anti-Shadow Weapon." Which, of course, made concealing her identity my job... Ah well. Thank you, old friend, for your understanding and your help; that decree from the Sixth Chamber was a considerable assistance.
As to the nature of these so-called "Shadows" and S.E.E.S.'s plans for fighting them, the children have not told me a great deal—though I gather that is because the information they themselves hold is quite limited. The good news is that Aigis has confirmed the "monsters" appearing in Laterano are not Shadows. I have sorted my conjectures about the nature of those monsters into roughly five directions; do look at the attachment. On balance, I consider the likeliest course of events to be that the "monsters" will cease activity once the students leave, or pass into a completely unobservable state.
More than the Shadows, what worries me is the state of these children. They are all still so young. They ought to be enjoying a quiet, peaceful life at school, yet they have already grown used to risking themselves against Shadows and treat it as a duty they must shoulder. For Aigis, who calls herself an "Anti-Shadow Suppression Weapon," perhaps that seems only natural—but as I see it, she has a real and precious life just as the other children do, and she too deserves the chance to know what life is truly worth, whether here or after they return. I hope she will come to have a life of her own, and that one day no one will call her a "weapon" again.
